article.headline: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Gains 193.4% This Year As Earnings Surge
article.deck: HPE broke out Oct. 1 from a 17-week deep cup with a 64.35 buy point and now trades 9.5% above it, extended past the 67.57 top of the buy range.
body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells the machines that sit under corporate, cloud and AI workloads. Its server line runs from ProLiant rack and tower machines to the Cray supercomputing systems, and the company also runs hybrid cloud, networking and financing businesses. In a year when buyers have chased AI hardware, that lineup has put HPE among the strongest stocks on the desk's list: shares are up 193.4% this year and 188.5% over 12 months.

The quarters show why. Earnings in the July quarter rose 404.8% to 1.06 a share, and revenue grew 33.7%. Per-share profit has climbed in each quarter shown, from 11 cents in the October 2025 quarter to 31 cents, 44 cents and then 1.06. Revenue dipped in the January quarter before rising in each of the next two.

The market still prices that growth modestly. HPE carries a market value of about $93.6 billion and trades at 14.97 times forward earnings, a lower multiple than Nvidia's 15.14 and well under Arista's 41.40.

On the chart, HPE broke out Oct. 1 from a 17-week deep cup with a 64.35 buy point. The base corrected 36.6% from a June 2 high to a July 2 low. The breakout came on volume just 0.79 times the 50-day average, below the turnout a proper breakout needs, but the stock has run anyway. Tuesday it rose 2.12, or 3.1%, to 70.48 on volume 0.78 times average, closing 9.5% above the buy point and past the 67.57 top of the buy range. It is extended.

The stock is 1.0% below its 52-week high of 71.22 and 24.6% above its 50-day line at 56.59; the 21-day line sits at 62.30. A year's low of 19.84 shows how far it has come. The relative strength line is at a new high, and HPE holds RS rank 96 of 99 on the desk's list. After hours the stock traded at 71.36, up 1.2%, as of 5:30 p.m. ET.

The news flow is steady rather than dramatic. HPE said it was chosen to deliver intelligent connectivity and autonomous IT operations at the 2027 Ryder Cup, and a Trefis piece Tuesday weighed HPE against Dell as a way to bet on AI hardware.
The entry is gone. A new base, or an orderly pullback to the 21-day line, would be the next point to judge the stock.
article.watch: A pullback toward the 21-day line at 62.30, or a new base that holds above the 64.35 buy point.

The buy range runs to 225.74, and the close sits 0.2% past the entry. Volume came in at 1.12 times the 50-day average, a light turnout for a breakout session.

The move came with the networking group. A 247 Wall St. headline Tuesday said Arista advanced 4% while Ciena soared 11% on AI networking demand, with Cisco up 3%. Arista was also named with Astera and GE Vernova among six AI stock buys in an evening market column as the S&P 500 hit a high.
A close back below 214.99 would turn the move into a stalled breakout.

article.headline: Nvidia Edges Higher, Holds Near Peak As Tech Giants Carry Rally
article.deck: Nvidia sits 1.1% above the 236.64 buy point of a 20-week cup, inside a buy range that runs to 248.47, though volume has not confirmed the move.
body: Nvidia added 34 cents, or 0.1%, to 239.24 Tuesday, holding a day after it cleared the 236.64 buy point of a 20-week cup. The base corrected 19.8% from its May 14 high to its June 29 low. Monday's breakout came on volume just 1.04 times the 50-day average, a bare turnout for a stock of this size, and Tuesday's trade dried up to 0.82 times average. The close sits 1.1% above the entry, inside a buy range that runs to 248.47.

The stock is 1.7% below its 52-week high of 243.37 and 8.9% above its 50-day line at 219.77, with the 21-day line at 227.17. The relative strength line sits 2.6% below its high, and Nvidia holds RS rank 74 of 99 on the desk's list, behind several chip peers. Shares are up 28.3% this year and 27.5% over 12 months.

Earnings in the July quarter jumped 127.8% to 2.46 a share on revenue growth of 105.9%. Per-share profit has risen in each quarter shown, from 1.30 in the October 2025 quarter to 1.76, 2.39 and 2.46, though the latest step was the smallest of the three. The next report is due Nov. 17.

Tuesday's tape matched a Yahoo Finance headline: markets climbed as a handful of tech stocks powered the rally. Nvidia rode along rather than led, adding a fraction of a percent while chip and networking names such as Astera Labs and Arista posted the big gains.
A close back under 236.64 would make this a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Whether volume picks up as Nvidia tries to take out its 243.37 high while holding above the 236.64 buy point.

article.headline: Thermo Fisher Slides 3% In Heavy Trade Despite New Clinical Trial Contract
article.deck: Thermo Fisher is still 1.9% above the 644.09 buy point of a 33-week cup and inside a buy range that runs to 676.29, but Tuesday's loss came on above-average volume.
body: Thermo Fisher fell 20.18, or 3.0%, to 656.58 on volume 1.35 times the 50-day average, a heavy-volume decline. The stock broke out Sept. 16 from a 33-week cup with a 644.09 buy point; that base corrected 32.4% from its Jan. 22 high to its May 18 low, and the breakout came on volume 1.5 times average. Tuesday's close sits 1.9% above the buy point and inside the buy range, which runs to 676.29.

Fourteen sessions after the breakout, the stock is 5.4% below its 52-week high of 694.33. It held above the 21-day line at 652.21 and sits 5.6% above the 50-day line at 621.56. The relative strength line is 9.3% off its high, and Thermo holds RS rank 74 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 13.3% this year and 28.7% over three months.

June-quarter earnings rose 9.3% to 4.68 a share, with revenue up 10.5%. The quarterly line is uneven: 4.27, 5.21, 4.43 and 4.68 a share across the quarters shown. That is single-digit profit growth behind a leadership-style chart. Results are due Oct. 21.

The day's news was operational. Quantum BioPharma signed a contract with Thermo's clinical research business to run a Phase 2 trial of Lucid-MS in multiple sclerosis, and the company showcased drug-development tools at CPHI Milan 2026. Neither headline accounts for the drop.
A close below 644.09 would put the breakout in trouble going into the report.
article.watch: Whether Thermo holds the 21-day line at 652.21 and the 644.09 buy point into the Oct. 21 report.

article.deck: Visa is 3.9% below the 385.67 buy point of a 6-week flat base after a bounce off its 50-day line; the buy range would run to 404.95.
body: Visa rose 93 cents, or 0.3%, to 370.64 on volume 0.54 times the 50-day average. The stock sits in a 6-week flat base with a 385.67 buy point. The base corrected 7.5% from an Aug. 26 high to an Oct. 2 low, and the buy range would run to 404.95. The close sits 3.9% below the entry.

Visa bounced off its 50-day line at 369.11 and closed just 0.4% above it; the 21-day line is at 367.29. The 52-week high of 385.57 marks the top of the base. The relative strength line is 9.7% below its high, and Visa holds RS rank 48 of 99 on the desk's list, in the bottom half. Shares are up 5.7% this year and 5.9% over 12 months.
June-quarter earnings rose 10.4% to 2.97 a share, with revenue up 14.4%. Per-share profit went from 2.62 in the September 2025 quarter to 3.03 and 3.14 before easing to 2.97. Results are due Oct. 27.

OpenTable and Visa extended their agreement in the U.S., Mexico and Canada. Separately, a Visa survey found nearly half of Asia Pacific consumers open to stablecoins, and a related headline said nearly half of people in Asia might use stablecoins by 2031.
A close below the 50-day line would undo the bounce; a lift in the RS line would be the first sign of new leadership.
article.watch: Whether Visa holds the 50-day line at 369.11 into the Oct. 27 report.

market_note: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7818.93 and the Nasdaq added 0.4% to 27599.79, with both indexes above their 50-day lines, by 1.9% and 4.5%. The Dow gained 0.5% to 51521.28 but remains 2.2% below its 50-day line. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Nasdaq 3 and the Dow 6, and the desk keeps the market at Uptrend under pressure. Leadership is narrow and chip-heavy: Astera Labs, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Palo Alto Networks, Zeta Global, Taiwan Semiconductor and Arista head this week's breakout list, the AI chip group has 92% of its names above the 50-day line against 14% for consumer stocks, and no desk name moved 3% or more after hours.
